text:
A feasible design is a preregistered 2×2 factorial: baseline/new architecture crossed with baseline/new objective, retaining all four datasets. Estimate architecture effects under each objective and their interaction; changing both simultaneously cannot isolate architectural benefit. Fix preprocessing seed=0, training seed=42, evaluation users/candidates, and checkpoint rules. Allocate equal GPU-second search budgets per cell within 43,200 GPU-seconds, counting diagnostics and failures; report training cost and completed updates because equal epochs need not mean equal compute. This design follows [factorial experimental principles](https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat503/Lesson05) and evidence that [fair comparisons must include tuning cost](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v119/sivaprasad20a/sivaprasad20a.pdf).

For uncertainty, retain each user’s binary hit and compare models on identical users and candidates. Bootstrap paired user outcomes within each dataset, then recompute the four-dataset macro difference; report its 95% interval and dataset effects. This applies [paired resampling principles](https://www.aclweb.org/anthology/P18-1128.pdf). With 200 users, one changed hit moves dataset HR@10 by 0.5 percentage points and macro HR@10 by 0.125 points. These intervals condition on trained models and fixed candidate samples; they exclude training-seed variability and do not establish full-catalog superiority. [Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) show sampled metrics can reverse model rankings, so preserve the pinned 99-negative evaluator and limit claims accordingly.

Checkpoint selection and repeated trial selection both optimize noisy validation estimates. Prespecify evaluation cadence, stopping, tie-breaking, comparison count, and search spaces; log every attempt and freeze the selected pipeline before the host’s held-out evaluation. Treat validation confidence intervals as exploratory after selection: bootstrapping selected predictions cannot remove tuning bias. [Cawley–Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html) document potentially substantial selection optimism.
